summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a five-day history of epigastric, right upper, and left upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and dark stools. She has a history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by marginal ulcers and a prior Clostridium difficile infection. On admission, she was started on IV fluids and pantoprazole. An EGD revealed a new small ulcer at the gastrojejunal anastomosis, improvement in a prior large ulcer, and resolution of a previous small ulcer. Pantoprazole was increased to twice daily, and sucralfate was continued. A CT abdomen and pelvis showed no obstruction or free air but noted a small area of hypoattenuation in the left kidney, possibly representing a small pyelonephritis or ischemia; however, urinalysis was normal. Stool tests for C. difficile and H. pylori were negative. Pain was initially managed with IV morphine, then transitioned to oral Roxicet, which was ineffective, and subsequently changed to oral Dilaudid with improved control. The patient tolerated a regular diet, hematocrit stabilized, and she was discharged home with instructions to continue medications, follow up with gastroenterology in six weeks for repeat EGD, and contact her surgeon within two weeks.
problems: Gastrojejunal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
